newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African exports to win U.S. renewal of GSP.
newsitem.headline: S.African exports to win U.S. renewal of GSP.

text.p: South African exporters stand to benefit from the U.S. Congress's decision to reauthorise the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) for developing and least developed countries.

The South African Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) announced on Tuesday the U.S. GSP would be renewed from October 1, 1996 to May 31, 1997, and would be retroactive from July 31, 1995 when the last programme expired.
A DTI spokesman told Reuters this meant all exporters who paid duty on exports to the U.S. would be refunded, plus interest, as long as their goods were cleared under GSP regulations.
The GSP programme provides preferential or duty free entry to the U.S. market for about 4,280 products.

Cape Chamber of Commerce and Industry deputy director Colin Boyes welcomed the move and said one of the major problems facing countries such as South Africa when they tried to get into developed country markets was non-tariff barriers.
"If the U.S. is opening up, this is to be encouraged as it will promote South Africa's economic growth," he said.
